content.text: I read every input file, all six figure briefs, the numeral ledger, and all ten draft sections, and traced each limitation, numeral, and figure statement back to the disclosure or to the one substantive USER passage in the conversation (the stirring-element/autonomous-mode message). Findings: none.

input.summary:
Complete ledger built and traced. AUTHORITY USED: input/disclosure.md plus the single substantive USER passage in input/conversation.md ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion", with "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand"); the other USER turns are operational (resume/regenerate/tighten wording) and were treated as non-disclosure, and no YOU/REVIEWER text was used as support. input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, and the "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support entries, all of which match draft/01, 02, 03.

CLAIMS: every limitation of claims 1-20 traced. Claim 1: rigid base with first/second sides, vibration motor coupled to first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, perimeter member at the perimeter of the second side surrounding the chamber ("The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material"); bearing face as the end face of that member and rigid contact ("maintaining rigid contact with the tile"); clearance admitting ambient air ("continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter"; "not intended to form a complete airtight seal"); extraction rate maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber ("maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere"); all-rigid, non-elastomeric transmission path ("connected to the tile through rigid components", "does not rely on flexible rubber or foam"); slidability under maintained differential ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"). Dependents 2-7 (closed loop restricting without sealing; plastic/metal/PTFE/combination; free of rubber, elastomer, foam; holding force without operator downforce; continuous extraction; vacuum pump) and 8-9 (guiding handles; rope/wire/cable pulling element) all map to explicit disclosure sentences. Claim 10 and the corresponding summary/description paragraph map to the stirring-element USER passage. System claims 11-15 and method claims 16-20 recite only limitations already traced, including the decoupled-control whereby clause ("the pressure differential independently supplies the force holding the device against the surface").

NUMERALS: all seventeen entries in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) are source-supported, each appears in the detailed description, each appears on at least one sheet, and each carries one meaning across sheets (24 = band/loop-legs/ring/column all being the perimeter member; 36 = tile/bottom band/uppermost band all being the covering element; 10 = the whole machine on FIGS. 1, 5, 6). No numeral appears in the text that is absent from the table, and the unused 28/30/32 gap introduces no orphan part.

FIGURES: FIG. 1-6 briefs depict only disclosed parts. Generic slabs, blocks, bands, the closed ring, and the rectangular plan form are marked schematic and disclaimed inside the briefs only; the application text and claims stay shape-neutral (no "rectangular", no "any closed outline", no "by way of example" broadening anywhere in draft/04-10). Functional-surface geometry checked specifically: the FIG. 4 bearing-face end line is disclaimed as to shape and asserts only the disclosed rigid contact and the disclosed clearance; the FIG. 2 passage through the slab verbalizes only the two endpoints of the affirmatively disclosed fluid communication ("in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base") with port, duct and valve construction disclaimed, and adds no depth, taper, angle, runout or contact-topology statement; FIG. 4's layer order (covering element on bonding material on substrate) matches "the bond between the tile and the underlying substrate", with extent of contact expressly not asserted; FIG. 6's count, form and position of stirring elements are disclaimed and no engagement with any body beneath is asserted.

CONSISTENCY: draft/07 matches each brief, including the repaired FIG. 2 enumeration (base, chamber, perimeter member and covering element in section; air-extraction mechanism in elevation; motor and handle omitted) and the FIG. 6 recital (single body, covering element omitted, only numerals 10 and 48). Section designations repeat identically in the resulting view, the source-view brief, and the drawing description: 2-2 appears in the FIG. 2 view line, on the horizontal line of FIG. 3, and in draft/07; 4-4 appears in the FIG. 4 view line, on the vertical line of FIG. 3, and in draft/07. FIG. 2 showing the perimeter member bearing on the covering element and FIG. 4 showing a clearance are reconciled by the "along at least part of the perimeter member" recital used identically in the claims and the description. Terminology is uniform across summary, description, claims and abstract. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any of the ten draft sections; the abstract is a single paragraph of roughly 144 words. No unsupported technical assertion or verified internal inconsistency was found, so the findings array is empty.

text: An exhaustive source-fidelity review was conducted. Every limitation in all 20 claims, every numbered part in the numeral list, and every technical assertion in the detailed description, abstract, and all six figure briefs was traced to an affirmative statement in the inventor's disclosure or subsequent USER messages. The draft is fully supported by the provided sources. The application is internally consistent: reference numerals are used consistently, terminology is uniform across sections, the brief description of the drawings matches the detailed figure briefs, and the claims are fully supported by the detailed description. No drafting notes, placeholders, or other non-filing text were found. The use of schematic views for structures whose appearance was not disclosed by the inventor is appropriately and consistently caveated in the figure briefs. The depiction of both contact and clearance between the perimeter member and the covering element is consistent with the disclosure and consistently explained in the text. The naming of inherent but unnamed features like the "bearing face" adds no new matter. The review is clean.
